title: Single-shift blitz retrospective: rapid incidents and follow-ups
content:
Shift summary (UTC):

Quick summary:
- Single overnight shift (02:00–10:00 UTC) turned into a high-density incident window: 3 mid-priority events overlapping, two required paging to L2. No customer-facing outages beyond transient elevated latency and a small spike in 5xx for hosted-api.
- Primary impact: transient tail-latency for text-generation endpoints (p95 -> 2.4s normally 0.8s) and a small group of customers with increased request timeouts.
- Root causes (initial): cache invalidation storm on edge-routing, autoscaler misconfiguration for a reserved pool, and disk pressure alert on a private cluster node group.

Timeline (concise):
- 02:07 UTC — Pager: API 5xx spike alert (threshold: 1% 5xx over 5m). First alert came from hosted-api-route-A.
- 02:10 UTC — Oncall (Aisha) triaged: sampled logs, saw rapid 503/504 tied to upstream inference pods returning OOMKill for some worker pods.
- 02:18 UTC — Notified L2 (Liam). Evidence: KV cache miss rate jumped, and a recent automated cache purge job ran 02:02 UTC with a bug causing wide invalidation.
- 02:25 UTC — Short-term mitigation: temporarily increased retry/backoff for client-facing router and throttled the purge job via feature-flag (feature-ops/purge-scheduler). Latency improved p95 -> 1.0s.
- 03:05 UTC — Autoscaler failing to scale reserved-gpu-pool-3: observed queueback and insufficient node provisioning; alert triggered.
- 03:12 UTC — Escalated to infra (Marcus). Root cause: the quota check in the autoscaler config referenced an outdated quota-id (quota tag deleted during housekeeping). Manual override provisioned 2 extra nodes; queue drained.
- 04:00 UTC — Private cluster node group alert: disk pressure on node-private-07; multiple system pods restarted. Investigated node disk usage and discovered old debug logs consuming /var/log/* (legacy fluentd config used).
- 04:40 UTC — Node cordoned and drained; pod replicas moved to healthy nodes. Longer-term fix scheduled.
- 06:20 UTC — Post-mitigations: system stabilized; background jobs re-enabled after cautious ramp (purge job re-enabled 06:50 UTC with throttling).

Immediate mitigations applied (what we did):
- Feature-flagged purge scheduler to emergency off. (feature-ops/purge-scheduler false)
- Increased client router retry/backoff window for 10 minutes to avoid cascading requests.
- Manually provisioned nodes into reserved GPU pool (infra console).
- Cordoned private node and rotated logging retention to free /var/log.
- Created short-term Grafana dashboard to track purge job run counts, KV miss rate, GPU queue depth. Link posted to #sre-oncall.

Runbook notes / deviations observed (patches we should add):
- Purge job runbook currently assumes small keyspace; it does not check list-length before global invalidation. Add guard: if keyspace > X or run frequency < 24h then require manual confirmation.
- Autoscaler playbook references quota IDs; add a periodic validation step that reconciles quota-ids against cloud provider and flags stale references.
- Private node logging retention was misdocumented; update node provisioning template to set logrotate and remove legacy fluentd rule that keeps verbose local debug logs.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- RD-2147 (Aisha) — Purge scheduler safe-guard and canary mode by 2026-04-22. (Jira: RD-2147)
- Infra checklist (Marcus) — Add autoscaler quota-id reconciliation job + alert by 2026-04-25.
- Ops/Provisioning (Sofia) — Update node bootstrap scripts to enforce logrotate and cap local log retention; create migration plan for private cluster nodes by 2026-04-24.
- Observability (Liam) — Promote the ad-hoc dashboard to a templated dashboard and add run-book links in Grafana panels by 2026-04-20.
- Post-incident customer comms (CS lead) — Draft a short note for impacted customers summarizing what happened and mitigations (coordinating with CS). Target: 2026-04-19.

Open questions / follow-ups noted during handoff:
- Why did the purge job run at 02:02 UTC? There is an automated schedule but schedule metadata looks unchanged. Need to confirm whether a config roll triggered a backfill run. (Investigate: infra/config-rolls 02:00–02:05)
- Are our retry/backoff knobs visible to customers? We temporarily raised them; need to ensure we don't inadvertently increase tail latency for low-tier customers. Decide if we should have tiered retry policies.
- Confirm whether node-private-07 had prior warnings (disk usage trend) that were missed. Add a retention alert threshold and a weekly trending job.

Notes to next shift (handoff):
- Watch the purge job schedule for any unexpected runs. Alert if run_count > 0 in the next 6 hours.
- Confirm that the temporarily provisioned GPU nodes are part of the reserved pool and will not be auto-removed by housekeeping. Tag: manual-provision-2026-04-18.
- Monitor p95/p99 for hosted-api-route-A and route-B for 12 hours post-mitigation; escalate to L2 if p99 > 5s for 5m.
- Follow-up with Marcus on quota recon job status; if not started, escalate to infra PM.

Communication artifacts and quick links (posted during shift):
- Slack thread: #sre-oncall "blitz 04/18" (pinned)
- Jira: RD-2147 (Purge scheduler), RD-2149 (Private node logging), RD-2150 (Autoscaler quota reconciliation)
- PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/389 — temporary change to purge scheduler (needs review + test)
- Grafana: ad-hoc dashboard link (posted in slack)

Lessons / heuristics learned:
- Large global invalidation jobs are brittle when combined with autoscaling events — consider batching or progressive invalidation instead of a single atomic sweep.
- Instrumentation gaps: keyspace size visibility at job runtime would have flagged risk earlier. Add a pre-flight estimate.
- Small config housekeeping changes (quota-id deletion) can have outsized effects if referenced by autoscale automation. Reconcile config references when deleting infra metadata.

Appendix: quick runbook excerpts used during mitigation (text only for drive doc)
- Emergency cache-pressure mitigation:
  1) Flag purge-scheduler = false (ops flag console)
  2) Increase router backoff: set ROUTER_RETRY_BASE=200ms -> 400ms for 10m window
  3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and 5xx rate
- Autoscaler quick fix:
  1) Validate quota-id: cloudcli quotas list -> ensure referenced id exists
  2) If missing, manual-provision nodes via infra console and create temporary reconciliation ticket
- Node disk pressure:
  1) cordon node -> kubectl cordon node-private-07
  2) drain with ignore-daemonsets; move pods to other nodes
  3) run cleanup: rotate logs and remove debug files older than 7d

Handoff sign-off:
- Oncall (Aisha) -> handing off to follow-up rotation at 10:00 UTC (primary: Liam).
- Slack: @Liam assigned follow-ups in thread, ticket created RD-2147 linked.

Document traceability: this is a working-note doc intended for quick handoff and follow-ups. Convert to a short incident review if follow-ups surface any persistent regressions.

-- end of note --
